title: Tierwise preset
description: Structure of a preset document (MANIFEST-19 to MANIFEST-36). A preset is a reusable set of kinds, naming patterns and lint settings that a project extends. Its top-level keys are the schema-file keys of SRC-14 plus lint, and it never contains extends (MANIFEST-35, MANIFEST-36). The schema checks shape only. Semantic checks stay in the compiler: duplicate definitions (SRC-39, SRC-40, SRC-43), invalid naming patterns and declarations (LINT-14 to LINT-17, reported as E_PRESET), lint settings that name engine error codes (LINT-8), and invalid lint names or severities (LINT-10). A preset is read only while compiling and is not part of the bundle (BUNDLE-109). It does not declare a spec version (MANIFEST-6).

decision_hierarchy.description: The decision hierarchy declaration (SCOPE area, section 2). A preset may declare it, and it is declared at most once across all sources (SRC-39).

entity_hierarchy.description: The entity hierarchy declaration (ENTITY area, section 3). Declared at most once across all sources (SRC-39).

facts.description: Fact declarations (FACT area, section 3). Each fact is declared at most once across all sources (SRC-40).

kinds.description: Kind definitions (KIND area, section 5). A kind defined here may be replaced by a later layer (MANIFEST-32).

naming.description: Naming patterns, a mapping from pattern name to an entry with category, pattern and optional description (LINT-14). A naming member that breaks this form is E_PRESET in a preset (LINT-14, MANIFEST-36). A pattern that a later layer redefines replaces the earlier one (MANIFEST-32).

keys.description: Key declarations (KEY area, section 5). Each key is declared at most once across all sources (SRC-40).

features.description: Feature declarations (FEAT area, section 7). Each feature is declared at most once across all sources (SRC-40).

namespace.description: The namespace key. MANIFEST-36 allows every key that SRC-14 allows in a schema file, and SRC-14 lists namespace, so the schema accepts it. No clause defines its meaning in a preset: NS-3 and NS-7 tie it to namespaced and shared schema files, and a preset is neither. This is an open point for the section 1 owner. Until it is ruled on, the compiler behaviour for namespace in a preset is undefined.

lint.description: Lint settings for the preset: a mapping whose only key is rules, which sets lint rule severities. A setting that names an engine error code is E_PRESET whatever its value (LINT-8). Severities resolve in layer order (LINT-4, MANIFEST-31).
